claims.text: Cold rolling followed by aging to introduce a secondary nano-precipitate phase will simultaneously increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The relevant as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase or eutectic microstructure.
Moderate cold rolling introduces dislocations into the alloy.
Moderate cold rolling refines the alloy microstructure.
A tailored aging treatment will nucleate and grow nano-precipitates at phase interfaces.
A room-temperature cold-rolling reduction of 20–30% is an appropriate controlled deformation range for the proposed treatment.
An aging temperature between 500°C and 600°C is typically appropriate, subject to selection using the alloy phase diagram.
A suitable aging duration can produce a uniform nano-precipitate dispersion without excessive coarsening.
The treatment will introduce nano-precipitates at grain boundaries and phase interfaces.
Cold work will produce grain refinement that acts as a structural mediator.
Nano-precipitates strengthen the alloy by impeding dislocation motion.
The refined grain structure increases grain-boundary strengthening.
The refined grain structure promotes more uniform plastic deformation and thereby enhances ductility.
The combined precipitation and grain-refinement mechanisms yield a better strength-ductility combination than the untreated state.
The treated alloy will have higher yield strength than the as-cast baseline.
The treated alloy will have higher elongation at fracture than the as-cast baseline.
The intervention is most applicable to eutectic high-entropy alloys with stable, well-defined dual-phase microstructures and interface chemistry amenable to controlled precipitation.
Substantial composition changes or phase instability at the treatment temperature may reduce the effect or require different processing parameters.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant increase in both yield strength and ductility relative to the as-cast control would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe the proposed nano-precipitate dispersion and refined grain structure would falsify the proposed mediator.
